what_it_does: DustNet is a wireless system for implanted neural recording devices. The challenge: surgeons need to wire up 4–8 tiny sensors implanted several centimeters deep in the brain, and they must all send data simultaneously at rates of 200–400 kilobits per second without spreading infection or requiring thick cables. DustNet solves this using ultrasound (similar to medical imaging) instead of radio waves. Each implant uses a technique called ASK backscatter modulation—it reflects the incoming ultrasound waves back in a controlled way to send its measurement data, like holding up a mirror and tilting it to signal in Morse code. Sixteen different reflection patterns let each implant encode 16 different signal levels per pulse.
